from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Defining the Sphere: From 1D to 3D",
            [
                "A sphere is all points at distance R from center.",
                "In 1D, a sphere is just two points on line.",
                "In 2D, a sphere is the boundary of circle.",
                "In 3D, it is the surface of solid ball.",
                "The boundary dimension is always one lower than space."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        center_dot = Dot(color=WHITE)
        radius = 1.5
        radius_line = Line(ORIGIN, [radius, 0, 0], color="#00FFFF")
        
        anim1_group = VGroup(center_dot, radius_line)
        self.place_in_area(anim1_group, "B2", "E5")
        
        rot_tracker = ValueTracker(0)
        radius_line.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_angle(rot_tracker.get_value()))
        
        trace = TracedPath(radius_line.get_end, stroke_color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=2)
        
        self.add(center_dot, radius_line, trace)
        self.play(rot_tracker.animate.set_value(2 * PI), run_time=3)
        radius_line.remove_updater(radius_line.updaters[0])
        
        self.play(FadeOut(anim1_group), FadeOut(trace))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        
        axis = Line(LEFT * 2, RIGHT * 2, color=WHITE)
        dot_minus_r = Dot(color="#00FFFF").move_to(LEFT * 1.5)
        dot_plus_r = Dot(color="#00FFFF").move_to(RIGHT * 1.5)
        
        dim1_group = VGroup(axis, dot_minus_r, dot_plus_r)
        self.place_in_area(dim1_group, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(axis))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_minus_r, scale=0.5), FadeIn(dot_plus_r, scale=0.5))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        
        circle_2d = Circle(radius=1.5, color="#00FF00")
        self.place_in_area(circle_2d, "C2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(axis, circle_2d),
            FadeOut(dot_minus_r),
            FadeOut(dot_plus_r)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#FFD700"))
        
        sphere_3d = Circle(radius=1.5)
        sphere_3d.set_fill(color=["#FFD700", "#B8860B"], opacity=0.8)
        sphere_3d.set_stroke(color="#FFD700", width=2)
        shine = Dot(radius=0.3, color=WHITE, fill_opacity=0.3).move_to(sphere_3d.get_center() + UP*0.5 + LEFT*0.5)
        
        sphere_group = VGroup(sphere_3d, shine)
        self.place_in_area(sphere_group, "C2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(circle_2d, sphere_3d), FadeIn(shine))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        
        notation = MathTex(r"S^{n-1} \subset \mathbb{R}^n", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(notation, "F2", "F5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Write(notation))
        self.wait(3)

            ]
        )

        COLOR_1 = "#00FF00" # Green
        COLOR_2 = "#FFFF00" # Yellow
        COLOR_3 = "#FFFFFF" # White

        # Display the 2D formula x^2 + y^2 = R^2 in green (#00FF00) at the center of the grid area.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_1)
        formula_2d = MathTex("x^2 + y^2 = R^2", color=COLOR_1)
        self.place_in_area(formula_2d, "C3", "D4", scale_factor=1.5)
        
        self.play(Write(formula_2d))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate the 2D formula morphing into x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \dots + x_n^2 = R^2 in yellow (#FFFF00).
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_2)
        formula_nd = MathTex("x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \\dots + x_n^2 = R^2", color=COLOR_2)
        # Using a slightly wider area to center the longer formula
        self.place_in_area(formula_nd, "C2", "D5", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        self.play(Transform(formula_2d, formula_nd))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Apply a pulsing white (#FFFFFF) highlight around the entire n-dimensional sum to signify its definition of distance.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_3)
        
        highlight_rect = SurroundingRectangle(formula_2d, color=COLOR_3, buff=0.2)
        self.play(Create(highlight_rect))
        
        # Pulse animation using ValueTracker to avoid always_redraw Text/MathTex issues
        # although here we just pulse a Rectangle which is simple.
        pulse_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)
        highlight_rect.add_updater(lambda m: m.scale_to_fit_width(formula_2d.width * pulse_tracker.get_value() + 0.4))

        self.play(pulse_tracker.animate.set_value(1.1), run_time=0.5, rate_func=there_and_back)
        
        self.wait(2)

        self.play(FadeOut(highlight_rect), FadeOut(formula_2d))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Volume Paradox: Shrinking to Zero",
            [
                "Unit sphere volume changes as dimensions increase.",
                "Volume peaks at dimension five then starts decreasing.",
                "In very high dimensions, the volume approaches zero.",
                "Compare a sphere inside a high-dimensional cube.",
                "The sphere occupies almost none of the cube's volume."
            ]
        )

        # Colors for lecture lines
        c1 = "#FFFFFF"
        c2 = "#00BFFF"
        c3 = "#00BFFF"
        c4 = "#00FF00"
        c5 = "#00FF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(c1))
        
        # V_n(R) = (pi^(n/2) / Gamma(n/2 + 1)) * R^n
        formula = MathTex(
            r"V_n(R) = \frac{\pi^{n/2}}{\Gamma(\frac{n}{2} + 1)} R^n",
            color=c1
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A1", "A6", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(c2))
        
        # Calculate volumes for n=1 to 10
        def get_volume(n):
            return (np.pi**(n/2)) / gamma(n/2 + 1)
        
        vol_values = [get_volume(n) for n in range(1, 11)]
        
        chart = BarChart(
            values=vol_values,
            bar_names=[str(i) for i in range(1, 11)],
            y_range=[0, 6, 1],
            y_axis_config={"font_size": 20},
            x_axis_config={"font_size": 20},
            bar_colors=[c2] * 10
        )
        self.place_in_area(chart, "B1", "F6", scale_factor=0.6)
        
        self.play(Create(chart))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(c3))
        
        # Animate bars for n > 5 shrinking rapidly towards zero.
        bars_to_highlight = chart.bars[5:] # n=6 to 10
        self.play(
            LaggedStart(
                *[bar.animate.set_color(WHITE).set_color(c3) for bar in bars_to_highlight],
                lag_ratio=0.2
            )
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(c4))
        
        vol_text = Text("Volume -> 0", color=c4, font_size=36)
        self.place_at_grid(vol_text, "D5")
        self.play(Write(vol_text))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(c5))
        
        # Scale the 'Volume -> 0' text up and down
        self.play(vol_text.animate.scale(1.5), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(vol_text.animate.scale(1/1.5), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(vol_text.animate.scale(1.5), run_time=0.5)
        self.play(vol_text.animate.scale(1/1.5), run_time=0.5)
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "Surface Concentration: The 'Thin Crust' Effect",
            [
                "High-dimensional volume concentrates near the surface.",
                "The interior of the sphere is mostly empty.",
                "Imagine peeling a hundred-dimensional orange.",
                "The thin peel contains nearly all the mass.",
                "There is no 'meat' in a high-D orange."
            ]
        )

        # Colors for lecture lines and elements
        c1 = "#FFFFFF"
        c2 = "#FF4500"
        c3 = "#FFA500"
        c4 = "#FFFFFF"
        c5 = "#FF0000"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # "High-dimensional volume concentrates near the surface."
        # "Draw a white unit circle (#FFFFFF) and a smaller concentric circle (#FF4500) at radius 0.95."
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(c1))
        
        outer_circle = Circle(radius=2, color=c1, stroke_width=2)
        inner_circle = Circle(radius=2*0.95, color=c2, stroke_width=2)
        circles_group = VGroup(outer_circle, inner_circle)
        self.place_in_area(circles_group, "B2", "E5")
        
        self.play(Create(outer_circle), Create(inner_circle))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # "The interior of the sphere is mostly empty."
        # "Gradually fade the center area of the circle to #000000 to show the 'empty' interior."
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(c2))
        
        # Using a solid circle to "fade out" the center by darkening it
        center_fill = Circle(radius=2*0.95, fill_color=BLACK, fill_opacity=0, stroke_width=0).move_to(inner_circle)
        self.add(center_fill)
        self.play(center_fill.animate.set_opacity(0.8), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # "Imagine peeling a hundred-dimensional orange."
        # "Fill the region between the circles with a bright orange color (#FFA500) to represent the 'crust'."
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(c3))
        
        crust = Annulus(inner_radius=2*0.95, outer_radius=2, fill_color=c3, fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0)
        crust.move_to(outer_circle)
        self.play(FadeIn(crust))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # "The thin peel contains nearly all the mass."
        # "Animate an arrow (#FFFFFF) pointing to the orange crust with the text 'Mass Concentration' in #FFFFFF."
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(c4))
        
        mass_label = Text("Mass Concentration", font_size=18, color=c4)
        # Position label at F1 and arrow pointing to the crust
        self.place_at_grid(mass_label, "F4", scale_factor=1.0)
        arrow = Arrow(start=self.grid["F4"] + UP*0.3, end=crust.get_bottom(), color=c4, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(GrowArrow(arrow), Write(mass_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # "There is no 'meat' in a high-D orange."
        # "Display the text 'No Meat at Center' in red (#FF0000) and then make it disappear to emphasize the emptiness."
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(c5))
        
        no_meat_text = Text("No Meat at Center", font_size=24, color=c5)
        self.place_at_grid(no_meat_text, "C3")
        
        self.play(Write(no_meat_text))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(no_meat_text))
        self.wait(1)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Setup the layout with title and lecture lines
        self.setup_layout("Applications: The Curse of Dimensionality", [
            "In high dimensions, points are usually far apart.",
            "This makes searching and organizing big data difficult.",
            "Geometry explains the challenges of modern AI models."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a set of points scattered in a 2D square (color #FFFFFF).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        num_points = 25
        points = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.06, color="#FFFFFF") for _ in range(num_points)])
        
        # Define the center of the right-side area
        area_tl = self.grid["B2"]
        area_br = self.grid["E5"]
        center = (area_tl + area_br) / 2
        
        # Generate random initial offsets within a small cluster
        np.random.seed(42)
        initial_offsets = [
            np.array([np.random.uniform(-0.6, 0.6), np.random.uniform(-0.6, 0.6), 0])
            for _ in range(num_points)
        ]
        
        # Initial placement of points
        for i, p in enumerate(points):
            p.move_to(center + initial_offsets[i])
            
        self.play(FadeIn(points))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Animate the points drifting apart to represent increasing sparsity in high dimensions.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # ValueTracker to control the "expansion" or "sparsity"
        spread_tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)
        
        # Persistent mobject update for efficiency
        def update_point_pos(p, idx):
            p.move_to(center + initial_offsets[idx] * spread_tracker.get_value())

        for i, p in enumerate(points):
            p.add_updater(lambda m, i=i: update_point_pos(m, i))
            
        # Drift apart over time
        self.play(spread_tracker.animate.set_value(4.5), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade in the title 'Curse of Dimensionality' in bold red (#FF0000).
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Creating the title once and placing it via grid
        curse_title = Text("Curse of Dimensionality", weight=BOLD, color="#FF0000", font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(curse_title, "A2", "A5")
        
        self.play(FadeIn(curse_title))
        self.wait(3)

        # Final color reset and hold
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Defining the Sphere: From 1D to 3D
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a sphere not as a 'ball,' but as a set of points at a fixed distance 'R' from a center. Review the progression: a 1D sphere (two points), a 2D sphere (a circle), and a 3D sphere (the surface of a ball). Emphasize the boundary vs. the interior.
sections.example: Visualize a 'Point-Bot' moving on a line (1D), a flat plane (2D), and in a room (3D). The boundary is always one dimension lower than the space it inhabits.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Multi-Dimensional Pythagorean Theorem
sections.content: Transition to the mathematical definition. If a 2D circle is x² + y² = R² and a 3D sphere is x² + y² + z² = R², an n-sphere follows the pattern x₁² + x₂² + ... + xₙ² = R². This is simply the distance formula extended to n-coordinates.
sections.example: Imagine a 'Hyper-Ant' crawling in a 4D space. To find its distance from the origin, it just adds the square of its 4th coordinate to the usual 3D distance formula.

sections.title: The Volume Paradox: Shrinking to Zero
sections.content: Explore how the volume of a unit sphere (R=1) changes as dimensions (n) increase. Use a graph to show that volume increases until n=5, then starts decreasing rapidly toward zero. In infinite dimensions, the volume of a unit sphere vanishes.
sections.example: A 'Shape-Shifting Box': If you put a circle inside a square, it takes up most of the space. But as dimensions increase, a hyper-sphere inside a hyper-cube occupies almost none of the cube's volume—it becomes a 'ghost' shape.

sections.title: Surface Concentration: The 'Thin Crust' Effect
sections.content: Explain a counter-intuitive property: In high dimensions, almost all the volume of a sphere is located in a very thin shell near the surface. The interior is essentially empty.
sections.example: The 'High-D Orange': If you peel a 100-dimensional orange, even a paper-thin peel contains 99% of the fruit's mass. There is practically no 'meat' in the center of a high-dimensional orange.

sections.title: Applications: The Curse of Dimensionality
sections.content: Relate these geometric oddities to modern technology. High-dimensional spheres explain why 'Big Data' is difficult to process (points are always far apart) and how AI models organize information in vector spaces.
sections.example: A Recommendation Engine (like Netflix): Each movie is a point in a 1000-dimensional space. Because of sphere properties, most movies are 'equidistant' on the surface, making it hard to find a 'nearest neighbor' without clever math.

storyboard.title: Defining the Sphere: From 1D to 3D
lecture_lines: A sphere is all points at distance R from center.
In 1D, a sphere is just two points on line.
In 2D, a sphere is the boundary of circle.
In 3D, it is the surface of solid ball.
The boundary dimension is always one lower than space.
animations: Show a central white dot (#FFFFFF) and a radius line (length R, color #00FFFF) rotating to define a set of points.
Draw a horizontal axis (#FFFFFF) and mark two points at -R and +R with bright blue dots (#00FFFF).
Transform the horizontal axis into a 2D circle outline (color #00FF00) with radius R.
Expand the 2D circle into a 3D sphere surface [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ball.svg] with subtle radial gradients (color #FFD700).
Display the mathematical notation "S^{n-1} \subset \mathbb{R}^n" in white (#FFFFFF) to emphasize the dimension drop.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: The Multi-Dimensional Pythagorean Theorem
lecture_lines: Pythagorean theorem extends to any number of dimensions.
We sum the squares of all coordinate values.
This defines the distance to origin in n-dimensions.
animations: Display the 2D formula x^2 + y^2 = R^2 in green (#00FF00) at the center of the screen.
Animate the 2D formula morphing into x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \dots + x_n^2 = R^2 in yellow (#FFFF00).
Apply a pulsing white (#FFFFFF) highlight around the entire n-dimensional sum to signify its definition of distance.

storyboard.title: The Volume Paradox: Shrinking to Zero
lecture_lines: Unit sphere volume changes as dimensions increase.
Volume peaks at dimension five then starts decreasing.
In very high dimensions, the volume approaches zero.
Compare a sphere inside a high-dimensional cube.
The sphere occupies almost none of the cube's volume.
animations: Display the unit sphere volume formula V_n(1) = (\pi^{n/2}) / \Gamma(n/2 + 1) in white (#FFFFFF).
Generate a bar chart (#00BFFF) for n=1 to n=10; animate the bars growing until n=5.
Animate the bars for n=6 to n=10 shrinking significantly to show the decline toward zero.
Draw a white square (#FFFFFF) and an inscribed circle (#00FF00); label them 'Cube' and 'Sphere'.
Scale the circle down slightly and change its opacity to 0.1 to show it 'occupies almost none' of the cube.

storyboard.title: Surface Concentration: The 'Thin Crust' Effect
lecture_lines: High-dimensional volume concentrates near the surface.
The interior of the sphere is mostly empty.
Imagine peeling a hundred-dimensional orange.
The thin peel contains nearly all the mass.
There is no 'meat' in a high-D orange.
animations: Draw a white unit circle (#FFFFFF) and a smaller concentric circle (#FF4500) at radius 0.95.
Fill the region between the circles with a bright orange color (#FFA500) to represent the 'crust' and incorporate the orange icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/orange.svg].
Gradually fade the center area of the circle to #000000 to show the 'empty' interior.
Animate an arrow (#FFFFFF) pointing to the orange crust with the text 'Mass Concentration' in #FFFFFF.

Display the text 'No Meat at Center' in red (#FF0000) along with the meat icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/meat.svg] and then make it disappear to emphasize the emptiness.

storyboard.title: Applications: The Curse of Dimensionality
lecture_lines: In high dimensions, points are usually far apart.
This makes searching and organizing big data difficult.
Geometry explains the challenges of modern AI models.
animations: Create a cluster of 20 white dots (#FFFFFF) at the center of the screen, incorporating the data icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/data.svg] to represent the data distribution.
Animate the dots moving rapidly toward the edges of the frame to represent increased distance in high-D.
Fade in the text 'Curse of Dimensionality' in bold red (#FF0000) at the center of the now-empty space along with the robot icon [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/robot.svg].
